spec: C05-BUILD-SPEC.md 交付物 8 (hook JSON 双反斜杠, E7 形态) — KNOWN-PROBLEMS.md P8 'fast-path 对 /./、/../、8.3 短名放行(E7)'
escapingDiscipline: Per PMM lesson [tooling:hook-fixture-must-carry-producer-escaping] (2026-09-14 fast-path incident: a hand-typed-via-shell fixture had its double backslashes silently halved before ever reaching the hook, so the real E7 bug was never exercised) and [tooling:node-e-inline-strips-backslashes-in-claude-bash], this fixture's file_path value MUST be constructed by the runner entirely inside a .cjs file executed via `node <file>` -- string.replace(/\\/g,'\\\\') producing a JS string whose ACTUAL runtime bytes contain two literal backslash characters per path separator -- then handed to JSON.stringify()/spawnSync's stdin Buffer with no shell layer in between (never via a Bash heredoc, `node -e`, or any shell-interpreted string). This is a fixture-construction discipline note for the runner code, not a static file (the double-backslash path is inherently dynamic -- it embeds the isolated root's own mkdtemp path -- so it cannot be baked into a static JSON string here without re-introducing exactly the escaping risk this note warns against).
description: tool_input.file_path, after hook.cjs's JSON.parse, contains a literal DOUBLE backslash between every path segment (e.g. C:\\Users\\...\\decisions.md as an actual 2-char-per-separator string value) -- simulating an upstream client that double-escaped an already-escaped Windows path. resolveRepoRel()'s `fp.replace(/\\/g,'/')` turns each doubled backslash into a doubled forward slash (C://Users//...), which core.matchCanonical()'s path.win32.normalize()-based pipeline still collapses correctly, so isMemory resolves true. Only the shadow hook is a relevant consumer -- index-emit never receives a single file path. Expect: a shadow log line is appended (never silent) and isMemory resolves true (correct judgment). KNOWN DEFECT discovered empirically (reported, not fixed): the SAME resolveRepoRel() prefix-match gap as winpath-unc-admin-share/expect.json applies here too -- rel/repo both come back null because the doubled-slash fp never exact-prefix-matches HOME's single-slash form, silently skipping gate-blocking-list filtering and push-candidate computation for this event, even though it is correctly logged and correctly classified as memory. This fixture asserts only isMemory + non-silence, not repo/rel correctness.
